message.content:
### Building a New Desktop PC – A Step‑by‑Step Guide  

Below you’ll find everything from pre‑purchase research all the way through to turning your machine on for the first time. Feel free to skip sections that already apply to you; this list covers most common scenarios (gaming, content creation, office work, etc.).

---

#### 1️⃣ Define Your Purpose & Budget  
| Use Case | Typical Specs | Rough Price Range |
|----------|---------------|-------------------|
| **Gaming** | GPU ≥ RTX 3060 / RX 6700 XT, CPU i5/i7/AMD Ryzen 5/7, 16–32 GB RAM | $800–$2000+ |
| **Content Creation** | Multi‑core CPU (i9/Ryzen 9), ≥ 32 GB RAM, high‑end GPU (RTX 3080/TX) | $1500–$4000+ |
| **Office / Light Work** | Integrated graphics, i3/Ryzen 3, 8 GB RAM | <$500 |
| **General Home** | Mid‑range CPU/GPU combo, 8–16 GB RAM | $600–$1200 |

*Tip:* Make a spreadsheet listing each component’s price and performance rating so you can see where you’re getting value.

---

#### 2️⃣ Pick Core Components  

| Component | What to Look For | Why It Matters |
|-----------|------------------|----------------|
| **CPU** | Cores × Threads, IPC, TDP | Determines overall speed + multitasking ability |
| **Motherboard** | Socket compatibility, chipset features (PCIe lanes, M.2 slots, USB ports), BIOS support | Must match CPU socket; future upgrade path |
| **RAM** | Capacity, DDR4 vs DDR5, Speed (MHz), CAS latency | Faster memory improves gaming & productivity |
| **GPU** | VRAM size, CUDA cores / Stream processors, Memory bandwidth | Drives rendering/gameplay quality |
| **Storage** | SSD type (NVMe vs SATA), capacity, read/write speeds | NVMe gives fastest boot/load times |
| **Power Supply Unit (PSU)** | Wattage, 80 Plus certification, modular cables | Reliable power delivery & cable management |
| **Case** | Size (ATX/Micro‑ATX/E‑ATX), airflow, noise level, aesthetics | Houses components & affects cooling |
| **Cooling** | Stock cooler vs aftermarket air/liquid | Keeps temperatures low under load |
| **Operating System** | Windows/Linux/macOS (via Hackintosh?) | Depends on software ecosystem needed |

> **Pro Tip:** If you plan to overclock or run multiple GPUs, choose a motherboard with robust VRM design and plenty of PCIe x16 slots.

---

#### 3️⃣ Gather Accessories & Peripherals  

- Thermal paste (if not pre-applied)
- Cable ties / Velcro straps
- Anti‑static wrist strap (optional but recommended)
- Screwdrivers (Phillips #0/#00)
- Clean room wipes or microfiber cloths
- Monitor(s), keyboard, mouse, speakers/headset

---

#### 4️⃣ Prepare Workspace  

1. Find a clean, flat surface—ideally an anti‑static mat.  
2. Keep the area well lit.  
3. Have a small container ready for screws and tiny parts.  
4. Turn off and unplug all equipment before starting.

---

#### 5️⃣ Assemble Inside the Case  

##### 5.1 Install the Power Supply  
- Align PSU fan toward intake/exhaust depending on case layout.  
- Secure with screws; route main cables out of the back panel.

##### 5.2 Mount the Motherboard  
- Place standoffs into the case tray matching the board’s screw holes.  
- Carefully lower the motherboard onto them.  
- Tighten all screws evenly.

##### 5.3 Insert the CPU  
- Lift the CPU socket lever.  
- Line up the corner markers (triangle on CPU ↔ triangle on socket).  
- Gently drop it in; lock the lever down.  
- Apply thermal paste (a pea‑size dot works best).

##### 5.4 Attach the Cooler  
- Follow manufacturer instructions (air cooler mounting brackets or liquid cooler pump/block installation).  
- Connect the fan/pump header to the appropriate CPU_FAN or PUMP header on the motherboard.

##### 5.5 Add RAM  
- Unlock DIMM slot keys.  
- Snap sticks firmly until click sounds confirm secure seating.

##### 5.6 Slot the Graphics Card  
- Remove corresponding expansion slot covers at rear.  
- Slide card into topmost PCIe x16 slot; press until latch clicks.  
- Secure with screws.  
- Connect required PCIe power connectors from PSU.

##### 5.7 Install Storage Devices  
- Mount NVMe drives directly onto M.2 slots using supplied screws.  
- For SATA SSD/HDD, insert into drive bays and connect data + power cables.

##### 5.8 Wire Everything Together  
- **Data cables:** SATA/SAS cables → storage devices.  
- **Power cables:** 
  - 24‑pin ATX to motherboard.  
  - 8‑pin EPS to CPU.  
  - 6/8‑pin PCIe to GPU.  
  - SATA power to drives.  
- Route cables neatly behind the motherboard tray; use zip ties to keep them tidy.

##### 5.9 Front Panel Connections  
- Refer to the motherboard manual for exact pinouts.  
- Common connections: Power button, reset switch, HDD LED, front audio jack, USB headers.

---

#### 6️⃣ First Boot & Basic Setup  

1. Double‑check all connections.  
2. Plug monitor, keyboard, mouse, and power cord.  
3. Switch on PSU then turn on the system via the case button.  
4. Enter BIOS/UEFI immediately (usually `Del` or `F2`).  

   *In BIOS*:  
   - Set correct boot order (USB/DVD > internal disk).  
   - Enable XMP profile for RAM.  
   - Verify detected hardware matches expectations.  
   - Save changes and exit.

5. Create a bootable USB stick with your chosen OS installer (Windows Media Creation Tool, Ubuntu ISO, etc.).  
6. Boot from USB, install OS following prompts.  
7. Once installed, plug in internet, let drivers auto‑install, then download official driver packages:

   - NVIDIA/AMD GPU drivers  
   - Chipset/motherboard drivers  
   - Wi‑Fi/Bluetooth firmware (if applicable)

---

#### 7️⃣ Post‑Build Tweaks & Testing  

| Task | How To Do It | Reason |
|------|--------------|--------|
| **Benchmarking** | Launch 3DMark, Cinebench R23, Passmark | Establish baseline performance |
| **Stress Test** | Prime95 (CPU), FurMark (GPU), MemTest86 (RAM) | Check stability & temperature limits |
| **Temperature Monitoring** | HWMonitor, MSI Afterburner, Speccy | Ensure temps stay within safe ranges |
| **Cable Management Review** | Re‑tuck loose cables, add more tie‑downs | Improves airflow & looks cleaner |
| **BIOS Update** | Download latest version from vendor site | Adds bug fixes & feature improvements |
| **Backup Plan** | Clone primary drive or set up cloud backup | Protect against data loss |

If anything crashes during stress tests, double‑check voltages, reseat components, or consider upgrading cooling.

---

#### 8️⃣ Safety Reminders  

- Always ground yourself (anti‑static wristband or touch metal part of chassis).
- Avoid touching exposed pins or contacts while powered on.
- Never force a component into place; check alignment first.
- When working inside the case, ensure no wires block fans or vents.

---

#### Quick Checklist Before You Hit “Start”  

☑ All major components seated correctly  
☑ PSU connected to motherboard, CPU, GPU, drives  
☑ Data cables attached properly  
☑ Front panel switches wired right  
☑ Cooling solution secured and functioning  
☑ Case closed, no loose screws or stray cables  
☑ External peripherals plugged in  

Once satisfied, flip the switch! 🎉

---

### Need Help With Specific Parts?

Feel free to tell me:
- Your intended usage (gaming, editing, everyday tasks).  
- Desired budget range.  
- Any brand preferences or constraints (e.g., only AMD CPUs).  

I can suggest a tailored bill of materials or help troubleshoot any hiccups along the way. Happy building!
